title: Costume Party Pooper
logline: On Halloween, Pam signs up for a secret painting class, Michael shows up as Jan, and Jim's hologram prank on Dwight gets a Stamford-sized upgrade.
outline: A: Pam secretly signs up for a Tuesday watercolor class and tells no one, while Michael nearly catches her and Jim's hologram call sets up the prank. B: Michael goes as Jan to win Jan's approval and the office's love; Dwight and Andy both dress as Michael and fight over who is the real one; Toby says the candle hat is a fire code problem. C: Jim and Pam's fake David Wallace hologram prank on Dwight escalates when Karen joins from Stamford and Andy breaks into song; Stanley vents to Creed. Order: cold, A, B, C, A, B, C, A, B, C, A, tag.
theme: Who do you choose when you finally have to choose? Being loved means being present.
storySoFar: Halloween at Dunder Mifflin Scranton. Jim is in Stamford, calling and emailing Pam; Karen Filippelli keeps appearing in his messages, and Pam has heard about a dinner. Pam's unanswered card and her drafts stay in the drawer. Pam now has a secret: a Tuesday watercolor class at the Community Center, which she has told no one. Roy keeps pushing the June 14 wedding. Michael covered for Pam once and says he won't lie for her again. Michael runs Love Board 2.0 with Dwight and Andy as co-chairs who hate each other; Andy won Chair Day over Dwight, and Dwight still wants that chair. Jan visited on Chair Day Friday and offered Pam a Stamford transfer, which Michael refused. Michael dresses as Jan for Halloween. Jim and Pam's prank on Dwight, a fake David Wallace hologram call at 3 p.m., has grown with Karen's help. Stanley is at 189 days.

stateChanges.progress: Pam secretly signs up for a Tuesday watercolor class and tells no one, not even Jim. The card is still unanswered. Jim's hologram prank has her feeling guilty.

stateChanges.arc: Michael Wants to Be the Favorite
stateChanges.progress: Michael dresses as Jan for Halloween and calls it a compliment; Angela bans it, Toby objects to the candle hat, and Michael hands out candy that says 'favorite.' He tries to be present for Toby, who says 'be present' again.

stateChanges.arc: Dwight vs Andy for Number Two
stateChanges.progress: Both dress as Michael on Halloween and each claims to be the real one. Andy wins the sing-along; Dwight takes over the hologram and wants the chair.
Stanley at 189 in the tag; Michael's joke dies on silence and Kevin closes it out.

stateChanges.text: Stanley's countdown: 190 in the cold open, 189 in the tag; Michael's 'That's what she said' dies on silence each time.
Kevin: 'Nobody say nothing.' closes the cold open and the tag.
Andy's bear-paw phone plays banjo hold music; Oscar: 'Actually, that's a banjo on hold.'
Jan calls Michael's behavior disgusting when he is kind; the office now calls his Jan costume disgusting too.
Pam's painting class is on Tuesdays at the Scranton Community Center; she hasn't told Jim. Michael now knows and says he's not Jim, and promised to keep quiet, or maybe not.
Jim's Halloween hologram prank on Dwight: Karen joined from Stamford and made it a Stamford production. Dwight may go to Corporate's hologram call next week and find out.

scenes.recap: Stanley arrives in street clothes as his costume, Michael's joke dies on silence, and Kevin closes it out.

beats.text: I'm going as myself. A man who has been himself for 190 days.
Ooh, scary. Very scary. That's what she said.

beats.caption: Stanley stares at the copier
hands Michael a laminated Halloween safety card

beats.text: Who ate the candy out of my bowl? It was a bowl of mystery and I was the mystery.
Nobody say nothing.

beats.caption: Michael looks at the bowl. It is empty.

scenes.recap: Pam dressed as a painter again hides a class flyer, and Michael tries to get it out of her.

beats.text: I'm going as a painter. Same as last year.
You could be anything, Pam. You picked a smock.

beats.caption: folds a flyer into the pocket of her paint smock

beats.text: A painter again! You're the Mona Lisa of reception.
Thanks, Michael.
What's that in your pocket? A Stamford brochure? Is Jim sending you brochures?
It's a recipe.

lines: It's a beginner watercolor class at the Community Center. Tuesdays, six to eight.
I signed up this morning. I haven't told anyone. Not Jim. Especially not Jim.

beats.text: Recipes are my favorite. Pam, if you ever want to talk about a recipe, I'm your guy.

beats.caption: Pam smiles at her keyboard

scenes.recap: Angela lays down the Halloween rules, and Michael reveals that he's going as Jan.

beats.text: The Party Planning Committee has rules. No gore, no weapons, and no hats with fire.
Rules are for people who aren't going as me. I'm going as Jan. Black suit, grey wig, candle hat.

beats.caption: Everyone looks at Michael

beats.text: That is so disgusting.
She called me sweet last week. Sweet and disgusting. I'm taking it as a compliment.
Actually, you're going as your girlfriend. That's worse than disgusting.
Jan is not a costume. Denied.
I'm appealing.

lines: Halloween is about showing people who you really are.
I'm going as the most powerful woman I know. If she sees it, she'll understand what I'm saying.

beats.text: Kelly and I are doing a hayride subcommittee. Angela, you can join us or not.
There is no subcommittee. There is a committee.

scenes.recap: Dwight reads a fake David Wallace email about a 3 p.m. hologram, and Andy's bear-paw phone plays banjo hold music.

beats.text: Question: Why would David Wallace want a hologram of me at three o'clock? False. He wants a hologram of an Acting Regional Manager.
Dwight, that's a hologram. Cornell has a hologram too. It's in the library.

beats.caption: bear-paw phone starts playing banjo hold music

beats.text: Actually, that's a banjo on hold.
190 days. Somebody shoot me, but gently.

lines: David Wallace does not send an email before three. That's a rule I made.
Jim is on my list. He's in Stamford, which makes him a suspect on principle.

beats.text: Do not mention the hologram to Michael. He will try to be in it.

scenes.recap: Kelly pushes Pam about Karen and Jim's dinner, and Pam hides her class time on a napkin until Michael walks in.

beats.text: Is it true Karen is cooking Jim dinner? Like, a Stamford bride dinner?
Karen is nice.
Nice. Such a nice word. It's like a sweater with no seams.

beats.caption: writes Tuesday, 6 p.m. on a napkin and folds it twice

beats.text: Is that a recipe? I love recipes. I have a recipe for a life.
It's pumpkin bread. For a class.
What class? Are you taking a class? Pam, I can keep a secret. I'm a regional manager.

beats.caption: Pam says nothing

lines: It's painting. It's not a bread class. I don't know why I said bread.
Michael can't keep a secret. He keeps everything he hears in his chest like a leaky pen.

beats.text: I'm not Jim. You can tell me anything.
Thanks, Michael.

scenes.recap: Michael hands out candy with notes to win the office, while Dwight and Andy argue over who is the real Michael.

beats.caption: stands by the copier in a black suit, grey wig and candle hat

beats.text: False. Jan is not a costume. Andy, you are also not Michael.
I'm the Michael with the Cornell patch. I'm the most Michael.
You're both me. It's the best day of my life. Two of me, one of you.

beats.caption: Dwight and Andy stare at each other across the bullpen
hands out candy with handwritten notes that say 'You're my favorite'

beats.text: Is candy for me?
For everyone. Except Toby.
Your candy has a note that says 'favorite.' You cannot say favorite on a candy.

lines: Dwight is Michael's assistant. I'm Michael's Regional Director. We're dressed as the same guy, which is awkward for both of us.
Okay, it's fine. He's a good sport. He's not a good sport.

beats.text: Question: Are you going to sit in the chair again? False. You are not.
Chair Day was fair. You erased my tally.

scenes.recap: Jim appears as a hologram David Wallace, Karen joins from Stamford, and the prank turns into a three-minute production with Andy singing.

beats.text: Question: Is that David Wallace?

beats.caption: flickers into view on the conference screen, wearing a silver blanket

beats.text: Dwight. It's David Wallace. You're doing great, Acting Regional Manager.
Mr. Wallace! Sir! I am ready!
Stamford's watching. We want you to be the Acting Regional Manager of Halloween.
Hey! I'm the Regional Manager. Of Halloween. I'm the Halloween manager.

beats.caption: starts an a cappella 'Acting Regional Manager' jingle with Stamford's name in it

lines: We were going to do one minute. Dwight, a fake David Wallace, a silver blanket.
Karen made it a three-minute production. Stamford has a choir now.

beats.text: I'd rather be in Stamford.
Jim, they love it. Wave at them.

scenes.recap: Roy arrives dressed as a lumberjack and asks about Jim's call, and Pam admits the prank has gone too far.

beats.text: I'm a lumberjack. Also I'm the guy getting married June 14.
You're a lumberjack.
Did Jim call?

beats.caption: The reception phone is quiet

beats.text: Not yet. He's on the TV at three. He's a hologram.
A what?

lines: The prank was a three. Karen made it a nine. I wrote the email.
Dwight looked so happy. I think that's the worst part.

beats.text: Pam, your face is doing a thing.
It's not a thing.
Have you ever painted anything?
Yes. I'm going to paint on Tuesday.
Pam, you can't paint.
I can.

scenes.recap: Michael gives Toby a Serenity by Jan candle as a sign of affection, and Toby says it isn't in the fire code and asks him to be present.

beats.text: Toby, you're my favorite. Don't tell the others.
I'm not on your favorites list, Michael.

beats.caption: holds out a Serenity by Jan candle, cinnamon scented

beats.text: That's not in the fire code.
Actually, the candle hat is a fire code violation. Also the candle.

lines: Toby's card said 'be present.' I'm trying. I'm here.
I'm not wearing the candle hat for me. I'm wearing it for the office.

beats.caption: Michael takes the candle back

beats.text: Be present, Michael.
Okay. I'm present. I'm so present.

scenes.recap: Stanley vents to Creed about his countdown, and Creed says something unsettling that nobody follows up.

beats.text: 190 days. I count them out loud like a rosary.
I once got a pumpkin to talk. It said nothing. That was the scary part.

beats.caption: Stanley looks at the dumpster

beats.text: The man in the Tulsa pumpkin patch knew too much about wood.
Okay.

lines: Michael makes the same joke about my countdown every day. It dies every day.
I'd miss it. Don't tell him.

beats.text: Did I stutter?
I haven't said anything, Stanley.

scenes.recap: Pam shows Michael her Halloween painting and tells him she's signing up for the class, and Michael promises to keep quiet, or maybe not.

beats.caption: unrolls a watercolor of the office in costume, Michael in a grey wig

beats.text: Is that me? Am I the candle?
That's the Jan one. You look good.
Pam, I'm going to ask. Are you going to tell Jim about the class?
No. I'm going to tell me first.
I won't cover for you.
I didn't ask you to.
I'm just saying. I'm not going to tell him. I might tell him.
Actually, Michael has never kept a secret for longer than an elevator ride.

scenes.recap: After hours, Michael tries the countdown joke one more time and Kevin closes it out.

beats.text: Your countdown is getting shorter. That's what she said.

beats.caption: Silence in the empty office

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.
